thread:
alex.cust: Hi team — after upgrading to @redwood/sdk-node v1.5.0 our Next.js builds started failing in CI (esbuild + pnpm). Local dev works, but production builds on Vercel show a 401 at runtime when calling the API. Repro steps: 1) pnpm build, 2) deploy, 3) serverless functions crash with 401 from Redwood when importing the SDK. Logs: 
```
Error: Request failed with status code 401
 at createError (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/core/createError.js:16:15)
 at settle (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/core/settle.js:17:12)
 at IncomingMessage.handleStreamEnd (/workspace/node_modules/axios/lib/adapters/http.js:260:11)
```
I suspect bundler/exports map shenanigans — we use ESM+SSR. Any quick ideas?

julia.support: Thanks for reporting — can you paste your package.json and the minimal import line you use? Also which Node and pnpm versions? :eyes:

alex.cust: Sure — node 18.16.0, pnpm 8.9.0. package.json snippet: 
```
{
  "name": "cust-webapp",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk-node": "^1.5.0"
  }
}
```
And import: `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk-node'` (then `const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })`). Build succeeds but runtime call -> 401 from service. Locally with `next dev` it works.

sam.devex: Could be that the deployed bundle is resolving to the browser entry (which strips auth headers) or the package.json exports map points at an ESM file missing the Node runtime shim. Do you have a reproduction repo you can share? If not, can you run `node -p "require('@redwood/sdk-node/package.json').exports"` in CI environment?

alex.cust: No public repo. Ran that command in CI and got: 
```
{
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
So exports map looks normal.

julia.support: Thanks — can you also show the built artifact resolution? In the serverless runtime, run `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/sdk-node')"` (or `import.meta.url` equivalent). If it resolves to a browser/esm path that drops headers, that'd explain 401s.

alex.cust: Doing `node -p "require.resolve('@redwood/sdk-node')"` in the build environment returns `/vercel/path0/node_modules/@redwood/sdk-node/dist/esm/index.js`

nick.eng-runtime: That is the issue — serverless is resolving the ESM entry at runtime which our ESM build incorrectly bundles a browser-oriented fetch wrapper that doesn't include the auth header fallback for SSR. We're seeing this specifically for frameworks that set "type": "module" + certain bundlers (esbuild/rollup) where CJS fallback is not used.

sam.devex: Short term workaround: force resolution to the CJS entry. Options: 1) change import to `import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk-node/dist/cjs'` (not ideal), 2) pin to v1.4.2 which shipped different exports map, 3) add a resolver alias in your bundler: `alias: { '@redwood/sdk-node': '@redwood/sdk-node/dist/cjs' }`.

alex.cust: Can confirm aliasing to CJS fixed prod for us. Not ideal long term though. Any ETA on an official fix?

nick.eng-runtime: We're patching this. Root cause: our ESM build used a minimal fetch wrapper that assumes browser fetch semantics (no automatic auth header injection in some server runtimes). We'll ship a compatibility layer that ensures Node SSR picks up the auth shim and that package exports include a `node` conditional to prefer `./dist/node/esm.js` for Node environments. Tentative patch release: v1.5.1 in ~48 hours.

julia.support: We'll escalate internally and mark this HIGH for any customers using serverless + ESM. @nick.eng-runtime can you add a diagnostics snippet support can ask customers to run? Would be helpful for triage.

nick.eng-runtime: Added — please ask customers to run the following in their CI/runtime where they see 401s and paste output: 
```
node -e "console.log('NODE_VERSION', process.version)"
node -e "console.log('RESOLVE', require.resolve('@redwood/sdk-node'))"
node -e "console.log('EXPORTS', JSON.stringify(require('@redwood/sdk-node/package.json').exports, null, 2))"
node -e "const mod = require('@redwood/sdk-node/dist/esm/index.js'); console.log('HAS_FETCH_WRAPPER', !!mod.__isBrowserFetch)"
```
This will tell us whether the deployed code is hitting the ESM browser wrapper. (The `__isBrowserFetch` flag is a temporary internal probe we shipped in 1.5.0).

alex.cust: Running those now — output: 
```
NODE_VERSION v18.16.0
RESOLVE /vercel/path0/node_modules/@redwood/sdk-node/dist/esm/index.js
EXPORTS {".":{"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"},"./package.json":"./package.json"}
HAS_FETCH_WRAPPER true
```
So yep, confirmed.

julia.support: Thanks — we’ll note your case. Workaround (alias to CJS) is a good stopgap. We'll notify you when v1.5.1 is published. If you want, we can open a priority support ticket for CI rollback assistance.

ci-bot: Automated note: created support-ticket #SUP-1421 -> engineering assigned: nick.eng-runtime.

nick.eng-runtime: Follow-ups for engineering: 1) add a node conditional in package.exports so Node resolves to node-specific ESM with proper authshim; 2) add a short-term patch that toggles `__isBrowserFetch` to false in server builds; 3) add a doc note in SDK migration guide about bundler pitfalls and recommended alias until patch lands.

sam.devex: I'll draft the docs snippet and a sample esbuild alias: 
```
// esbuild config snippet
alias: {
  '@redwood/sdk-node': require.resolve('@redwood/sdk-node/dist/cjs')
}
```
And a Next.js next.config.js rewrite: 
```
module.exports = {
  webpack: (config) => {
    config.resolve.alias['@redwood/sdk-node'] = require.resolve('@redwood/sdk-node/dist/cjs')
    return config
  }
}
```

alex.cust: Thanks all — alias applied and prod is green. Will wait for 1.5.1. Appreciate the quick triage. :heart:

julia.support: Marking thread resolved for now; re-open if anything else pops up after patch. :white_check_mark:
